item.title: Frustrated Topological Orbital Magnetism
item.description: arXiv:2610.12557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By studying the interplay of geometric frustration with Aharonov-Bohm fluxes in three dimensions, we unveil a rich playground exhibiting topological semimetallic ground states with orbital magnetic dipole, quadrupole and ferrotoroidic orders, akin to spin patterns in classical spin ices - a class of phenomena which we dub frustrated topological orbital magnetism. We demonstrate that the ground-state toroidizations underpinned by non-Abelian topological nodal lines induce measurable current-induced Hall phenomena. We further find that distinct 2-in-2-out and 3-in-1-out frustrated orbital current patterns can be associated with topological Weyl node charges, and corresponding anisotropic linear and nonlinear Hall effects. We propose signatures for experimental validation of distinct frustrated topological orbital magnetic orders in candidate materials.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Garrido Bourkhaeva, Claudio Castelnovo, Wojciech J. Jankowski

item.title: Entropy Production in Mesoscopic Electronic Transport Beyond Weak-Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.12652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the full statistics of entropy production in coherent mesoscopic conductors beyond the weak-coupling regime. Using the inside-outside perspective and the Landauer-B\"uttiker scattering framework, we relate entropy production to the full counting statistics of particle transport and show that the corresponding cumulant-generating function satisfies the fluctuation symmetry independently of the coupling strength. We obtain closed analytical expressions for the cumulant-generating function in the weak- and strong-coupling limits, enabling a detailed characterization of entropy production distributions and higher-order cumulants. These cumulants reveal distinct signatures of resonant transport and coherent fermionic partitioning. While coupling-induced broadening substantially modifies the transport statistics, the fluctuation symmetry imposed by microscopic reversibility remains preserved in the long-time limit.
item.dc:creator: Ivana R. A. C. Lucena, Caio H. Lewenkopf, Alexandre R. Rocha

item.title: Electron binding by charge disorder surrounding gapped bilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.12714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bilayer graphene (BLG) is a unique electronic material offering electrostatic tunability of its band gap. Here, we study how charge disorder in the dielectric environment modifies band-edge states by binding electrons and holes to Coulomb centres, taking into account the in- and out-of-plane dielectric response of Bernal bilayers. We apply this framework to (a) hBN-encapsulated medium-size-gap BLG used for gate-defined quantum dots, and (b) BLG under double n/p ionic gating. In hBN/BLG/hBN, we find that single remote charges produce only weakly bound states, with binding energies generally small compared with the BLG gap. Under ionic gating, we find that the bound states are too large to be trapped by individual ions -- localisation arises from fluctuations in the ion density, whose magnitude is limited by Coulomb charging energy at the freezing temperature $T_f$ of the ionic configuration. Thus, in both regimes, charge disorder does not produce deep midgap states, with the bound states remaining closer to the conduction and valence band edges.
item.dc:creator: Jude McClay, Angelika Knothe, Igor Rozhansky, Vladimir Fal'ko

item.title: Nonlocal Josephson coupling and current redistribution in a large-area graphene multiterminal Josephson junction
item.description: arXiv:2610.12753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. We reproduce the NDLR response with a network containing the interplay between two distinct forms of nonlocality: nonlocal Josephson coupling, which determines the switching sequence of the superconducting network, and nonlocal normal-state conductance, which redistributes current after different regions switch. Our results highlight the potential of the emergent NDLR for characterizing superconductor--semiconductor hybrid systems and for nonlinear circuits. Further, this Josephson Hall bar geometry provides a platform for exploring the interplay between mesoscopic superconductivity and many-body ground states in graphene-based heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Luojia Zhang, Kushagra Aggarwal, Jay D. Sau, Ethan G. Arnault, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Valla Fatemi

item.title: Vacuum-field-mediated Landau-level reconstruction in a cavity-coupled two-dimensional electron gas
item.description:
arXiv:2610.12956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-dimensional electron gas in the integer quantum Hall regime coupled to a single spatially modulated cavity mode in the static off-resonant limit. Retaining both paramagnetic and diamagnetic contributions on equal footing, we derive a gauge complete single-particle Hamiltonian in which virtual photon exchange generates a periodic kinetic renormalization and a diamagnetic scalar potential. Both terms transfer momentum by $2k_0$ and displace guiding centers by $\Delta X=2k_0\ell_B^2$, forming a finite-$k_0$ momentum ladder. Diagonalizing the strip Hamiltonian, we find that the ladder reconstructs the Landau-level band structure and redistributes, rather than multiplies, the associated chiral edge states. Occupied-subspace Chern numbers remain $C_
u=
u$ for $
u=1,2,3$ throughout $0\le\lambda_{\mathrm{cav}}\le 0.5$, while the bulk gaps decrease without closing. Strip Kubo responses show cavity-induced displacements of the Hall-step energies; at finite width the plateau heights are noninteger and approach the integers as $L_x$ increases. The ladder is spectrally resolved at $k_0\ell_B=0.5$ and collapses at $k_0\ell_B=0.1$. These results isolate a spatially local, finite-$k_0$ momentum ladder as a clean-system mechanism by which a structured vacuum field reconstructs quantum Hall spectra and strip transport without changing the integer topology, complementary to cavity-mediated all-to-all hopping.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Heng Zhu, Yu Chen

item.title: Parity-Anomalous Hall Response of Chiral Lifshitz Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The parity anomaly of a single massless Dirac fermion is manifested as a half-quantized Hall response once the required parity-breaking regularization is supplied. We study the corresponding response for two-dimensional chiral Lifshitz fermions. For a node with low-energy coupling (qx +iqy)^N, the Fermi-loop winding number W = N gives an anomalous Hall response {\sigma}xy^anom = (W/2)e^2/h. We examine this mechanism in chiral multilayer Haldane models tuned to a valley-selective critical line, where a single gapless chiral Lifshitz fermion remains at the K valley. For the AB, ABC, and ABCA stacks, the projected pseudospin textures give W = 2, 3, 4, while Kubo calculations yield {\sigma}xy = (1, 3/2, 2)e^2/h; integrated equilibrium boundary currents reproduce the same W/2 sequence. Six-terminal simulations with dephasing further show that the Hall conductivity is quantized at W/2 while the longitudinal conductivity remains finite. These results identify gapless chiral Lifshitz fermions as a higher-order, winding-controlled generalization of the parity-anomalous Hall response, distinct from a quantum anomalous Hall insulating state even when W/2 is an integer.
item.dc:creator: Yanmiao Han, Rundong Zhao, Yu-Hao Wan

item.title: Orbital transfer reveals material-selective structure in Rydberg excitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.13149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg excitons in atomically thin semiconductors offer a sensitive view of dielectric screening and electronic structure. As their spectra become increasingly well resolved, a central question is how much material information an effective Hamiltonian can predict beyond the states used to determine it. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. After separating gap and common-scale contributions, the residuals reveal distinct material-dependent orbital patterns and constrain simple multichannel descriptions. For WS2, the measured 2p/3p curvatures yield a parameter-fixed prediction, Q4p=+4.08 meV, for a future same-platform measurement. Together these results show how a well-performing spectral model can be tested for transferable physical information, with the next unmeasured state providing an independent experimental check.
item.dc:creator: Mengli Wang, Peng Chen, Wenqi Xue, Haonan Xia, Hong Zhang, Benniu Zhang

item.title: Equal-Spin local and nonlocal Andreev reflection in altermagnet/superconductor/altermagnet junction
item.description: arXiv:2610.13193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigated the equal-spin Andreev reflection phenomenon in an altermagnet/super\-conductor/altermagnet (AM/SC/AM) junction, focusing on the roles of the crystal orientation angle and the N\'eel vector. The crystal orientation angle in the AM effectively determines the spin-dependent transport channels for both electrons and holes, leading to orientation-dependent local and crossed Andreev reflection in the AM/SC/AM junction. We studied how and under what conditions this equal-spin Andreev reflection occurs. Rotating the N\'eel vector in the AM substantially increases spin-flip channels for both electrons and holes, giving rise to equal-spin Andreev reflection. When the N\'eel vector $\theta=\pi/2$, the spin-dependent transmission channels for crystal orientations $\alpha=0$ and $\alpha=\pi/2$ are completely the same, the Andreev reflection coefficients remain different, reflecting the distinct roles of the N\'eel vector in spin space and the crystal orientation in real space. By tuning the crystal orientation angle and the N\'eel vector, orientation-dependent conventional and equal-spin Andreev reflection can be realized. This study reveals that N\'eel vector rotation is the direct cause of equal-spin Andreev reflection in AM/SC/AM junctions and provides a viable pathway for realizing spin-dependent superconducting transport phenomena in AM heterojunctions.
item.dc:creator: Kai-Yi Lyu, Xing Wang, Yu-Xian Li

item.title: Graphene double quantum dot as a solid-state two-level system in the THz range
item.description: arXiv:2610.13196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matter-based two-level quantum systems are fundamental building blocks of quantum technologies, underpinning applications in quantum computing, simulation, communication, and sensing. Today, most of these two-level quantum systems, including Rydberg atoms, trapped ions, superconducting circuits, molecules, and quantum dots, involve transition frequencies in microwave or optical domains. However, extending their transition frequency to the THz spectral range could provide numerous benefits, leveraging the unique properties of THz radiation. Here, we show that an hBN-encapsulated graphene double quantum dot realizes a two-level system with a transition frequency in the THz spectral range. Using low-temperature transport spectroscopy in the dark combined with modeling based on nonequilibrium Green's function formalism, we demonstrate the formation of an artificial molecule, featuring bonding and antibonding states separated by an energy of up to 0.6 meV, corresponding to a resonance frequency of 0.145 THz. This approach provides direct access to important parameters of open double quantum dot systems, including tunneling rates, offering a practical alternative to conventional techniques such as photon-assisted tunneling, which are challenging to implement at THz frequencies. The realized 2D-material-based THz two-level system, compatible with direct on-chip integration, could serve as a key building block for future THz quantum technologies. Furthermore, by involving a single-electron transition, coupling these devices to a THz resonator could enable the exploration of ultra-strong light-matter interactions at the fundamental limit of a single transition coupled to a single cavity, beyond the reach of existing THz quantum systems based on collective transitions.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Wietzke, Solen Coeymans, Benjamin Hue, Simon Messelot, Aurelien Schmitt, Michael Rosticher, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jerome Tignon, Sukhdeep Dhillon, Rebeca Ribeiro, Audrey Cottet, Matthieu Delbecq, Takis Kontos, Juliette Mangeney

item.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions in crystalline systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moir\'e effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.
item.dc:creator: L. Maisel Licer\'an, H. T. C. Stoof

item.title: Atomic Edge Resonators Flatten Phonon Bands in Biphenylene Nanoribbons
item.description: arXiv:2610.13342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that H--F edge complexes in biphenylene nanoribbons act as intrinsic atomic resonators, flattening low-frequency phonon branches. With increasing wave vector, flexural and twisting vibrations concentrate at the edges while motion of the carbon backbone is suppressed. Displacement profiles and edge-mass tuning identify a local-resonance mechanism, an atomic counterpart of a tuned mass damper. Combining machine-learned interatomic potentials, frozen-phonon calculations, and density-functional tight binding, we find that weakly dispersive modes contribute substantially to thermal band-gap narrowing. Zero-point motion shifts the calculated gap closure toward the experimentally observed ribbon widths. A hexagonal boron nitride substrate preserves the principal spectral features while reducing thermal renormalization. These results establish edge chemistry as a route to nearly flat phonon bands and connect a local atomic resonance to the electronic response of an entire nanoribbon.
item.dc:creator: V. L. Katkov, N. M. Chtchelkatchev, V. A. Osipov

item.title: Pulse-by-pulse imaging of reversible, collective reshaping in laser-excited gold nanorods
item.description: arXiv:2610.13383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanomaterial properties are governed by atomic structure, and driving structural changes on demand could enable materials with programmable properties. Pulsed light is the most controllable route: wavelength, fluence, polarization and pulse timing can each be tuned to inject energy with nanometre and picosecond precision and mould atomic positions. Yet the spatiotemporal dynamics of these transformations have remained hidden, inferred only from before-and-after snapshots. Here we track gold nanorods in a transmission electron microscope under pulsed optical excitation, quantifying the structural transition frame by frame. The rods enter an unexpectedly dynamic regime: material redistributes within and between particles, twin boundaries nucleate and propagate, rods hundreds of nanometres apart reshape in concert, and individual rods almost vanish before recovering their original shape, indicating a structural memory. Driving and following these transformations with pulse-synchronized in situ electron microscopy could turn light-induced reshaping into a tool for setting structure, and consequently properties, on demand.
item.dc:creator: Mees Dieperink, Loriane Monin, Ichiro Ohnishi, Takeo Sasaki, Yu Jimbo, Erik Garnett, Wiebke Albrecht

item.title: Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ with a Monolayer hBN Spacer
item.description: arXiv:2610.13493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted van der Waals heterobilayers are a promising material platform for studying collective exciton many-body phenomena, but near-aligned structures often exhibit a local, anisotropic atomic reconstruction that compromises lateral homogeneity. The present study describes how atomic-scale rearrangement in adjacent regions of hBN-encapsulated, near-aligned MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers is controlled by the presence of a mono- or bilayer hBN spacer between the two monolayers. High-angle annular dark-field STEM directly resolves the atomic alignment in both layers and shows that the spacer suppresses the reconstruction and strongly increases the structural uniformity of the heterobilayers. 4D-STEM quantitatively maps local rotation, dilation, and heterostrain, revealing that the separated regions remain consistent with rigid moir\'e superlattice simulations, whereas without the spacer the structural parameters have two to three times broader distributions. By suppressing reconstruction, ultrathin hBN spacers therefore provide an effective route to enhance lattice homogeneity in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers targeting collective excitonic and optoelectronic phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Figueiredo, Kaiyuan Chen, Aubrey Penn, Mirco Troue, Sebastian Loy, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Frances M. Ross, Julian Klein, Alexander W. Holleitner

item.title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
item.description: arXiv:2610.13542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,\mu$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moir\'e heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Igor Veremchuk, Pavlo Makushko, Anita Guarino, Muhammad Waqee Ur Rehman, Rosalba Tatiana Fittipaldi, Tobias Kosub, Alexej Pashkin, Fabian Ganss, Oleg A. Petrenko, Proloy T. Das, Rui Xu, Rhonald Burgos Atencia, Debottam Mandal, Antonio Vecchione, Carmine Ortix, Denys Makarov

item.title: Parametric Glassiness in Graphene-based Electronic L\'evy Glass
item.description: arXiv:2610.13638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex disordered conductors can display highly structured and parameter-sensitive transport even in the absence of a thermodynamically stable glass phase. Overlap distributions originally developed for replica symmetry breaking (RSB) provide a useful diagnostic of this organization, provided that their interpretation is distinguished from the equilibrium Parisi construction. In this study, we report RSB-like overlap phenomenology and parametric mesoscopic glassiness in a graphene-based electronic L\'evy glass, a device that mimics optical phenomena via electronic processes. By tuning the Fermi energy, we can control the number of propagating wave modes and observe reentrant changes from narrowly centered to broad or bimodal overlap distributions. The phenomenology is observed in both graphene-based and conventional two-dimensional electron-gas electronic L\'evy glasses, indicating its generality. Sample-resolved overlap distributions show that the effect is intrinsic to each disorder landscape, whereas the normalized conductance variance shows that the growth of the absolute variance is mainly caused by the increasing mean conductance. We therefore interpret the overlap as a measure of correlation among hierarchically organized transport pathways and the reentrant behavior as evidence of pinning, parameter-induced reorganizations, and mesoscopic chaos in coherent transport.
item.dc:creator: Caue N. da Silva, Diego B. Fonseca, Adauto J. F. de Souza, Ant\^onio M. S. Mac\^edo, Luiz Felipe C. Pereira, Anderson L. R. Barbosa

item.title: Cooper Instability of a Magnetic Wigner Crystal
item.description: arXiv:2610.10710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy has directly imaged electronic crystals in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, and magnetotransport measurements suggest that superconductivity and charge-density-wave order emerge from a common spin-valley-polarized ferromagnetic metal at nearby carrier densities. Motivated by these observations, we ask whether collective modes in a magnetic Wigner crystal can mediate pairing in this setting. We address this question by studying the Cooper problem for two electrons in the first conduction band of the Wigner crystal. Unlike conventional phonon-mediated pairing, the collective mode (boson) energies and single-particle (fermion) dispersion are comparable scales controlled by the electron density, leaving no small parameter for an adiabatic expansion. Moreover, because the magnetic Wigner crystal is not time-reversal invariant, the usual Cooper logarithmic divergence in the pairing susceptibility is absent, so the attraction must exceed a finite threshold for pairing to occur. These unusual features motivate a numerical experiment to see whether the crystal's own vibrations can bind electrons. We obtain the crystalline ground state and its collective mode spectrum within Hartree--Fock and time-dependent Hartree--Fock approximation, and derive the electron--phonon Hamiltonian using the quasiboson approximation. Solving the resulting two-electron problem, we find that phonon-mediated attraction exceeds the pairing threshold, with chiral $p$-wave pairing as the leading instability. Within these approximations, we show that collective modes of a Wigner crystal can indeed favor chiral pairing despite broken time-reversal symmetry. Our results provide an encouraging starting point for developing a full many-body theory to study electronic crystallization and superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Wangqian Miao, Chunli Huang

item.title: Flat-band quantum geometry from embedded quench dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.12555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum geometry underlies a wide range of correlated phenomena in electronic systems, yet accessing the geometry of individual bands remains experimentally challenging. Advances in quantum simulators, such as ultracold atoms in optical lattices, have enabled local state preparation and site-resolved measurements, offering direct access to quantum dynamics beyond conventional transport probes. These developments naturally raise the question of whether band-resolved quantum geometry can be extracted from local occupation readouts. Here, we propose an on-site quench protocol to probe the flat-band quantum geometry via local occupation measurements in an atomic lattice. Our scheme dynamically isolates the flat-band sector by coupling a one-dimensional flat-band lattice to a two-dimensional flat-band bath. The bath selectively removes dispersive excitations, while compact localized states remain trapped due to their overlap with the flat-band modes of the bath. We show that the late-time occupation pattern directly encodes the integrated overlaps between flat-band states separated by the wavevector of the initial density pattern, thereby enabling access to integrated quantum distances between the states separated by the commensurate momenta $\delta k = 2 \pi s/r$, $s,r \in \mathbb Z$ and to the integrated flat-band quantum metric. Our results thereby establish a direct connection between quantum geometry and the long-time memory of an initial spatial pattern in flat-band systems.
item.dc:creator: Ilia Komissarov, Daniel E. Sheehy, Ahana Chakraborty

item.title: Search for free non-Abelian anyons in paired composite-fermion states
item.description: arXiv:2610.12645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, understood as topological superconductors of composite fermions, are predicted to support elementary quasiparticles (QPs) or quasiholes (QHs) obeying non-Abelian braid statistics. Using the microscopic framework of parton theory, we investigate many experimentally observed paired composite-fermion states and find that their elementary QPs and QHs in general bind to form Abelian molecules, thus obscuring non-Abelian braid statistics. An exception is the $\nu=1/2$ state in wide quantum wells, where our calculations show free QPs or QHs; we thus identify this state as an especially promising candidate for realizing and studying non-Abelian braid statistics. We also indicate how the study of such bound states can help reveal the topological structure of the state.
item.dc:creator: Mytraya Gattu, J. K. Jain

item.title: The quantum geometry of the chemical bond
item.description: arXiv:2610.12746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electronic properties of materials depend both on band energies and quantum geometry of electronic states. We relate bonding indices to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), showing how chemical bonding dictates the momentum-space texture of bands, bridging chemical and physical descriptions of solids. We show the QGT decomposed into the three center bond index, weighted by their oriented area. Resolving these contributions by orbital pair reveals the donor--acceptor character that distinguish ionic, covalent, hypervalent, and metavalent bonding. We identify the bonding pattern for topology in materials: noncollinear three center bonds, which are the source of Berry curvature in solids. Bond fluctuation can be directly linked to electromagnetic response by resolving their energy spectrum, opening a quantitative route towards the design of physical properties of materials from bonding motifs.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Carrel, Nishchhal Verma, Fatmag\"ul Katmer, Leslie M. Schoop, Raquel Queiroz

item.title: Realizing Two-Dimensional Altermagnets with 100% Spin Polarization along the [110] Direction in Ambidentate-Ligand Based Square Organometallic Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.12791v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Altermagnetism, as a novel magnetic paradigm, not only possesses a zero net magnetic moment, but also exhibits a substantial nonrelativistic spin-splitting effect. Currently, developing a simple and experimentally feasible method for designing altermagnets is eagerly pursued. Moreover, achieving 100% spin polarization along certain directions in valence or conduction bands for altermagnets remains challenging. To address these issues, based on a tight-binding model, we propose a viable chemical strategy for constructing organometallic altermagnets by using ambidentate ligands. Furthermore, in these organometallic altermagnets, direction-dependent 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in band edges can be induced via the coexistence of altermagnetically spin-split dispersive and flat bands, where the flat band suppresses electron transport in one spin channel and the dispersive band enables conduction in the other spin channel. Then, via first-principles calculations, a screening of 90 two-dimensional ambidentate-ligand based square organometallic lattices leads to the identification of three altermagnetic materials, namely Fe(taz)2Cl2 (taz = 1,2,4- triazine), Co(app)2Cl2, and Fe(app)2Cl2 (app = 1,4-azaphosphinine), all of which possess 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in valence bands, as well as notable piezomagnetic behavior. This study paves the way for achieving direction-dependent fully spin-polarization in altermagnetic materials.
item.dc:creator: Qing-Bo Liu, Xin-Yi Chen, Xiangyang Li, Xingxing Li, Jinlong Yang

item.title: Ultrafast laser-stimulated field emission from a metal: a non-equilibrium Green's functions approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.13251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ultrafast laser-assisted field emission from metallic nanotips is a promising route for generating coherent electron pulses. However, existing theoretical models often neglect many-body strong correlation effects in the emitter's electronic structure and its response to the optical field. In this work, we propose a theoretical framework based on the non-equilibrium Green's function formalism to simulate the out-of-equilibrium electron dynamics across a strongly driven matter-vacuum interface, in a one-dimensional model. Treating the tip-vacuum coupling perturbatively, we find that the interplay between strong-field emission and multi-photon emission regimes can be described in terms of a filtering of the emitter's local density of occupied states through field-dressed vacuum propagators. By including electron-electron interactions via the second-Born approximation, we show that correlation-induced modifications in the electronic structure are directly transferred to the far-field spectrum. Finally, by self-consistently solving the Dyson equation at the interface, we uncover a dynamic back-action regime driven by the optical field, characterized by a periodic polarization of the emitter, which reshapes the far-field spectrum. This shows that the non-equilibrium Green's functions approach provides a versatile framework for exploring and analyzing field emission of correlated electrons.
item.dc:creator: Luciano Jacopo D'Onofrio, Adolfo Avella, Martin Eckstein

item.title: Predicting Nanofabrication Variance: A Conditional Diffusion Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.13420v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Micro- and nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam (FIB) milling invariably deviate from input designs due to systematic and stochastic effects such as ablation-rate fluctuations, and redeposition. As such, nominally identical iterations of a given process yield a distribution of non-identical fabrication outcomes, leading to variations in the physical (optical, mechanical) properties of fabricated structures. Existing models of the milling process typically predict a single deterministic fabrication result, neglecting this variability. Here we present a conditional diffusion model that learns the statistical distribution of process outcomes conditioned on input design, enabling it to predict a realistic distribution of possible output sample structures. These predictions accurately reproduce edge morphology, linewidth variations, and defect probabilities observed in fabricated samples, enabling statistical analysis of milling performance and the identification of dominant structural and process parameter-dependent deformation modes. The work establishes a probabilistic modelling framework for fabrication variability analysis and fabrication-aware design optimization.
item.dc:creator: Wenhan Zhang, Ben Mills, Oleksandr Buchnev, Kevin F. MacDonald

item.title: Domain-wall circulation gating and pinning via compositional engineering of cylindrical nanowires
item.description: arXiv:2405.00652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spintronic devices based on cylindrical magnetic nanowires have been proposed as a route toward three-dimensional information storage and processing by harnessing the controlled motion of domain walls (DWs). In this geometry, the Bloch-point wall (BPW) is the characteristic DW type. It features a curling of magnetization around a Bloch Point singularity, a topology that has been predicted to enable propagation at high speed without undergoing a Walker breakdown. We demonstrate that compositional modulations of larger magnetization, which host spontaneous curling states while the rest of the wire remains axial, fulfil a dual role: they act as deterministic pinning sites and as active gates for BPW circulation. Combining magnetic transmission X-ray microscopy and micromagnetic simulations, we reveal that DW-modulation interactions are the result of a superposition of long-range magnetostatic repulsion and short-range, circulation-dependent exchange contributions: parallel circulation produces an attractive well, while opposite circulation generates a repulsive barrier. This results in DW pinning at or near a compositional modulation. A DW's internal circulation can be inverted upon traversing a modulation, enabling on-demand switching of its circulation state. This dual mechanism demonstrates that both DW position and circulation can be tuned in a controlled manner, with potential implications for multistate spintronic devices.
item.dc:creator: L. \'Alvaro-G\'omez, C. Fern\'andez-Gonz\'alez, S. Ruiz-G\'omez, N. Mille, J. C. Toussaint, R. Belkhou, M. Foerster, E. Pereiro, L. Aballe, N. Bagu\'es, C. Thirion, D. Gusakova, A. Masseboeuf, O. Fruchart, L. P\'erez

item.title: Quantum Theory of Exciton Magnetic Moment: Interaction and Topological Effects
item.description: arXiv:2509.07284v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.
item.dc:creator: Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, Weichen Tang, Chen Hu, Mit Naik, Steven G. Louie

item.title: Anomalous Edge Contrast in Magnetic Force Imaging of 2D Topological Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2602.18281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic force imaging (MFM) of 2D topological insulators, such as crystalline plates of Bi2Te3 and Bi2Se3, reveals anomalously large contrast around the plate edges even under ambient imaging conditions. And while there are several known contrast mechanisms in MFM, these cannot easily explain the magnitude of contrast observe for such systems. In this work we use multi-parameter magnetic force phase imaging together with a simple analytical model to suggest that the observed magnetic edge-features can be associated with two sources: a pseudo-Faraday effect in the conductive edge channels of the topological system and magnetic scattering in those channels caused by the proximal, localized field of the tip. These results suggest novel MFM contrast mechanisms unique to topological systems and point to the utility of multi-parameter MFM techniques in studies of topological-material-based circuit elements.
item.dc:creator: Timothy W. Carlson, Motahhare Mirhosseini, Allison Swyt, Gabriel Marcus, Daniel Lazega, Scott McGuire, Lindsey J. Gray, Anthony Walsh, Swathi Kadaba, Maria Kolesnik-Gray, C. C. Dun, Vojislav Krstic, D. L. Carroll

item.title: Floquet-Multiple Andreev Reflections
item.description: arXiv:2605.02642v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Floquet theory describes quantum systems governed by time-periodic Hamiltonians, much as Bloch theory describes spatially periodic solids. In voltage-biased multiterminal Josephson junctions, the Josephson relation causes superconducting phase differences to evolve periodically in time, thereby providing an intrinsic Floquet drive. In this Letter, we consider three-terminal Josephson junctions formed on a ballistic two-dimensional normal conductor with a continuum of electronic states. We show that the quartet and higher-order multipair processes yield characteristic Floquet-multiple Andreev reflection (Floquet-MAR) finite-bias conductance and noise resonances that are parameterized by the bias voltage and electrochemical potential. This microscopic picture opens a route toward implementing and probing Floquet-MAR physics in ballistic multiterminal Josephson junctions.
item.dc:creator: R\'egis M\'elin, Romain Danneau, Morteza Kayyalha

item.title: Guidelines for band gap opening in graphene superlattices with periodic {\pi}-vacancy distribution
item.description: arXiv:2605.04900v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Periodic $\pi$-vacancies in graphene superlattices (GSLs) provide a symmetry-based route to band-gap opening in graphene by modifying the $\pi$-band dispersion. However, the symmetry conditions that determine whether a vacancy motif can open a band gap remain unclear. Here, we investigate periodic $\pi$-vacancy GSLs using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model with one $p_z$ orbital per carbon site to identify the symmetry requirements for gap opening. $\pi$-vacancies, representing functionalized, substituted, or missing carbon sites, are modeled as site deletions in the $\pi$ basis, with all hopping matrix elements to and from the deleted sites set to zero. We focus on $\pi$-vacancy motifs with $C_2$ and $C_3$ point-group symmetry. A $3n \times 3n$ GSL, where $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ is the integer scaling factor multiplying the honeycomb primitive-cell vectors, folds $K$ and $K'$ to $\Gamma$ and can therefore open a band gap. For $C_3$-type vacancies, the Dirac cones remain pinned at high-symmetry points and thus stay at $\Gamma$ in folded $3n$ GSLs. In contrast, $C_2$-type vacancies that reduce the global point group of the GSL to $D_{2h}$ by preserving a pair of perpendicular mirror symmetries, $\sigma_v \perp \sigma_d$, can also constrain the Dirac cones to $\Gamma$. When the $\sigma_v$ and $\sigma_d$ mirror planes are absent, the cones are allowed to shift away from $\Gamma$ to $(\pm \Delta q,\pm \Delta q)$ in the $3n$ superlattice.
item.dc:creator: Diyan Unmu Dzujah, Hongde Yu, Thomas Heine

item.title: Anomalous Transverse Thomson Effect
item.description: arXiv:2605.06299v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate the anomalous transverse Thomson effect (ATTE), the long-missing Thomson counterpart of the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst effects. Its coefficient is not unique but depends on the electrical boundary condition: $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(j)}$, defined for a spatially uniform imposed current density, and $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$, defined for equipotential electrodes. Both are fully determined by the total anomalous Nernst coefficient (ANC) and its temperature dependence, while $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$ acquires an additional contribution from the temperature dependence of the longitudinal resistivity. This relation is model independent within local linear response and applies to the total ANC regardless of whether its microscopic origin is intrinsic or extrinsic. Using a massive Dirac model for Fe$_3$Sn$_2$, we show that Berry curvature near the gapped Dirac cones enhances the ANC-related contributions to $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$. In the low-temperature limit, both $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(j)}/S_{xy}^{\rm A}$ and $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}/S_{xy}^{\rm A}$ approach a value of three. We further extract $\tau_{\rm ATTE}^{(E)}$ from reported experimental data for CoS\(_2\), Co\(_3\)Sn\(_2\)S\(_2\) and CeCrGe\(_3\); for CeCrGe$_3$ it reaches approximately -20 $\mu V/K$, and we estimate the maximum achievable cold-side heat current density to assess its cooling potential. Because the ATTE can be evaluated directly from existing ANC and longitudinal resistivity data, it is readily testable without additional equipment or measurements.
item.dc:creator: Ying-Fei Zhang, Zhi-Fan Zhang, Zhen-Gang Zhu, Gang Su

item.title: Contrasting $\Gamma$- and K-Valley Moir\'e Physics in Twisted Monolayer/Bilayer WSe$_2$
item.description:
arXiv:2607.18212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electronic orbital character plays a central role in determining electronic correlations, spin-orbit coupling, dimensionality, and ultimately the quantum phases of condensed-matter systems. Two-dimensional moir'e materials have emerged as highly tunable platforms for exploring correlated phenomena, but the role of orbital degrees of freedom remains largely unexplored. Here, we identify twisted monolayer/bilayer WSe$_2$ as a platform in which displacement-field tuning enables moir'e physics to be realized in both the $K$ and $\Gamma$ valleys. The distinct orbital characters of these valleys give rise to contrasting correlated phases at moir'e filling factors $
u=1$ and $
u=1/3$. At $
u=1$, the $K$-valley state is a weak insulator, consistent with an antiferromagnetic state near a van Hove singularity in the intermediate-coupling regime, similar to that observed in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$. In contrast, the $\Gamma$-valley state exhibits a pronounced Pomeranchuk effect, consistent with proximity to a Mott transition. At $
u=1/3$, the $K$ valley hosts a robust generalized Wigner crystal, whereas the $\Gamma$-valley state lies near the crystallization boundary and again exhibits a Pomeranchuk effect, with localization enhanced by increasing temperature or magnetic field. Our work highlights the importance of orbital character in defining quantum phases in moir'e systems, and identify the $\Gamma$ valley as a promising platform for exploring correlated phenomena near quantum phase transitions, where competing phases and enhanced fluctuations may give rise to unconventional phases.
item.dc:creator: Jackson Kuklin, Ning Mao, Milan Mandigo-Stoba, Edgar Elias, Tianci Song, Connor Engel, Pola Pietrzkowski, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Daniel Rhodes, Yang Zhang, Qianhui Shi

item.title: Josephson junctions, superconducting circuits, and qubit for quantum technologies
item.description: arXiv:2405.20911v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the realm of physics, a pivotal moment occurred six decades ago when Brian Josephson made a groundbreaking prediction, setting in motion a series of events that would eventually earn him the prestigious Nobel Prize eleven years later. This prediction centered around what is now known as the Josephson effect, a phenomenon with far-reaching implications. At the heart of this effect lies the Josephson junction (JJ), a device that has become a linchpin in various scientific applications. This chapter delves into the foundational principles of the Josephson effect and the remarkable properties of JJs. From their role in metrology to their application in radiation detectors, these junctions have ushered in a new era of electronics. Exploiting the unique features of superconductive devices, such as high speed, low dissipation, and dispersion, JJs find today practical implementation in the development of superconductive qubits and nanotechnology applications.
item.dc:creator: Roberta Citro, Claudio Guarcello, Sergio Pagano

item.title: Superconducting-antiqubit simulation enables optimal phase estimation via unitary inversion
item.description: arXiv:2506.04315v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A positron is equivalent to an electron traveling backward through time. Casting transmon superconducting qubits as akin to electrons, we simulate a positron with a transmon subject to particular resonant and off-resonant drives. We call positron-like transmons "antiqubits." An antiqubit's effective gyromagnetic ratio equals the negative of a qubit's. This fact enables us to time-invert a unitary implemented on a transmon by its environment. We apply this platform-specific unitary inversion, with qubit--antiqubit entanglement, to achieve a quantum advantage in phase estimation: consider measuring the strength of a field that points in an unknown direction. An entangled qubit--antiqubit sensor offers the greatest possible sensitivity (amount of Fisher information), per qubit, per application of the field. We prove this result theoretically and observe it experimentally. This work shows how antimatter, whether real or simulated, can enable platform-specific unitary inversion and benefit quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Xingrui Song, Surihan Sean Borjigin, Flavio Salvati, Yu-Xin Wang, Nicole Yunger Halpern, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur, Kater Murch

item.title: Specific-heat anomaly in frustrated magnets with vacancy defects
item.description: arXiv:2506.17392v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by frustrated magnets and spin-liquid-candidate materials, we study the thermodynamics of a 2D geometrically frustrated magnet with vacancy defects. The presence of vacancies imposes significant constraints on the bulk spins, which freeze some of the degrees of freedom in the system at low temperatures. With increasing temperature, these constraints get relaxed, resulting in an increase in the system's entropy. This leads to the emergence of a peak in the heat capacity $C(T)$ of the magnet at a temperature $T_\text{imp}$ determined by the concentration of the vacancy defects. The entropy associated with this peak comes from the lowest-energy degrees of freedom in the material. To illustrate the emergence of such an anomaly, we compute analytically the heat capacity of the antiferromagnetic (AFM) Ising model on the triangular lattice with vacancy defects. The presence of the vacancy leads to a peak in $C(T)$ at the temperature $T_\text{imp}=-4J/\ln n_\text{imp}$, where $J$ is the AFM coupling between the spins and $n_\text{imp}$ is the fraction of the missing sites.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Sedik, Siyu Zhu, Sergey Syzranov

item.title: Finite-Size Effects in Quantum Metrology at Strong Coupling: Microscopic vs Phenomenological Approaches
item.description: arXiv:2507.19994v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Equilibrium quantum metrology is often formulated under assumptions of weak system-bath coupling and thermodynamic limit scaling, which may not be valid for realistic finite-size (FS) quantum devices. Here, we establish how strong coupling (SC) and FS effects jointly modify achievable precision bounds for equilibrium quantum probes. Considering a transverse-field anisotropic XY spin chain coupled to a thermal environment, first utilize we derive a full polaron transform to derive the effective Hamiltonian at equilibrium. Then, using the bare Hamiltonian and the obtained effective Hamiltonian and taking into account the role of FS effects in the calculation of partition function, we derive an analytic expressions for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for a general parameter for the equilibrium state in weak coupling (WC) and SC regimes, respectively. In contrast to this microscopic approach, we also utilize the Hill's phenomenological nanothermodynamics to calculate an effective QFI expression at SC. Our results, presented for specific cases of magnetometry and thermometry, reveal that considering FS and SC effects lead to substantial and systematic deviations in QFI, even for moderate system sizes, and that commonly used thermodynamic-limit approximations can significantly misestimate precision. This work also highlights the inadequacy of phenomenological approaches in describing the metrological capability and thermodynamic behavior of systems at SC. Our work establishes a consistent framework for evaluating metrological performance of realistic, finite quantum devices operating beyond the weak-coupling paradigm.
item.dc:creator: Ali Pedram, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

item.title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
item.description: arXiv:2511.02440v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ultrafast all-optical magnetization switching (AOS) holds great promise for nextgeneration spintronic memory and hybrid spintronic-photonic systems. However, most implementations to date rely on bulky free-space optical setups, limiting scalability and practical integration. As a critical step toward integrated applications, we demonstrate single-pulse AOS within a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit. Using trains of femtosecond laser pulses guided through on-chip waveguides, we achieve deterministic toggle switching in a sub-micron out-of-plane Co/Gd Hall cross patterned directly atop the photonic waveguide. Electrical readout via the anomalous Hall effect reveals a switching contrast of up to 90% for 500 nm-wide devices. In larger Hall crosses, the contrast decreases and switching becomes stochastic, consistent with spatially non-uniform optical absorption as confirmed by finite-element simulations. This behavior is hypothetically attributed to domain wall relaxation and thermally assisted (de)pinning processes within partially switched regions. Our results highlight the critical role of device scaling in achieving robust on-chip AOS and establish a foundation for ultrafast, energy-efficient, and fully integrated spintronic-photonic platforms.
item.dc:creator: Pingzhi Li, Gijs W. A. Simons, Tianyu Zhang, Philip P. J. Schrinner, Sohrab Kamyar, Ronald Dekker, Diana C. Leitao, Reinoud Lavrijsen, Yuqing Jiao, Bert Koopmans

item.title: Engineering superconductivity on the surface of Weyl semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2604.26859v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ten years after the experimental discovery of Weyl semimetals, theoretical and experimental work has pointed to the possibility of realizing surface-only superconductivity at relatively high temperatures in these materials. A consensus is developing that this unusual form of superconductivity is supported by surface electronic states unique to Weyl semimetals, known as Fermi arcs. In this work, we show that the topological protection of these exotic states can be exploited to engineer high critical temperatures. Motivated by reports of van Hove singularities on the surface of PtBi$_2$-the first Weyl semimetal in which surface superconductivity was unequivocally linked to its Fermi arcs-we demonstrate how such singularities can be engineered through the deposition of a suitable additional layer. We find that the critical temperature becomes extremely sensitive to the exact value of the chemical potential, and values as large as 20 times the bulk $T_c$ can be achieved. More generally, our results demonstrate how topological protection can be exploited to manipulate surface electronic states, thereby opening experimentally accessible routes toward engineering high-temperature two-dimensional superconductivity and other exotic phases.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Vocaturo, Mattia Trama

item.title: DC Conductance of X-shaped Majorana Interferometer reveals Non-Abelian Anyon Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2607.24171v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a four-terminal, X-shaped chiral Majorana interferometer with a central floating superconducting island, enabling the direct detection of the non-Abelian statistics of Ising anyons via the linear-response DC conductance tensor in charge transport experiments. Here, Ising anyons are realizable as edge vortices nucleated at Josephson line junctions defining the superconducting island, where both edge-vortex and Majorana-fermion tunneling processes can occur. We show that in such a multi-terminal Majorana interferometer, both the vacuum and the fermionic fusion channel for Ising anyons are possible. This is in contrast to two-arm interferometers, where only the vacuum fusion channel is accessible and the DC conductance contribution from edge vortices always vanishes. Using a low-energy effective theory derived via chiral bosonization, we find that in the X-shaped interferometer, the DC conductance tensor is completely isotropic, yielding a non-zero conductance when simultaneous edge-vortex and Majorana tunneling activates the fermionic fusion channel. Apart from conductance oscillations in a gate-tunable charge parameter, which display an offset related to the anyon topological spin, measuring a finite conductance can already provide direct evidence for non-Abelian statistics in this geometry.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Giuliano, Andrea Nava, Reinhold Egger, Fabian Hassler
